skill.name: when-building-backend-api-orchestrate-api-development
skill.description: Guides production REST API development from requirements through deployment. It coordinates specialist agents across planning, architecture, TDD implementation, testing, documentation, and release validation.
skill.summary: Coordinate a complete REST API delivery workflow with TDD, quality gates, documentation, and deployment planning.
skill.author: DNYoussef

content.value_statement: Production API builds need clear roles, tests, and deployment gates. This skill organizes agents through planning, TDD implementation, validation, documentation, and blue-green release.
actual_capabilities: Defines a five-phase REST API workflow from requirements through monitoring.
Assigns product, architecture, database, QA, security, DevOps, and documentation roles.
Provides TDD steps for RED, GREEN, and REFACTOR implementation cycles.
Specifies validation gates for coverage, security, performance, documentation, and release readiness.
Includes a GraphViz process diagram for workflow visualization.
limitations: Does not implement an API without an agent runtime and project context.
Assumes access to claude-flow, test tools, deployment tools, and target infrastructure.
Command examples require review before use in production systems.
Uses generic Node.js and Kubernetes examples that may need adaptation.

use_cases.title: Plan a new service API
use_cases.description: Turn requirements into endpoints, data models, OpenAPI contracts, and a test strategy.

use_cases.title: Coordinate TDD implementation
use_cases.description: Guide backend, testing, and review agents through repeatable endpoint delivery cycles.

use_cases.title: Prepare release validation
use_cases.description: Organize security checks, performance tests, documentation, deployment, rollback, and monitoring tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Start an API plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new backend API.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this workflow to plan a REST API for my product. Define phases, agents, main deliverables, and first decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Design endpoints and tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the workflow to my requirements. Produce endpoint groups, data model tasks, OpenAPI tasks, and TDD test coverage goals.

prompt_templates.title: Run a TDD delivery cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Coordinate tester, backend developer, and reviewer agents for these endpoints. Keep the RED, GREEN, and REFACTOR outputs separate.

prompt_templates.title: Validate production readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the deployment phase to create a release readiness review with security, performance, documentation, rollback, and monitoring gates.

output_examples.input: Build a user management API with registration, login, profile updates, and admin user search.
output: A five-phase delivery plan with assigned agents and deliverables.
A TDD sequence for authentication and user management endpoints.
Quality gates for coverage, security review, documentation, and release approval.

output_examples.input: Prepare a payment API for production with strict security and performance targets.
output: A security-focused planning phase with PCI-related architecture tasks.
Parallel validation work for penetration testing, load testing, and documentation.
A release checklist covering rollback, monitoring, and support handoff.

output_examples.input: Create a microservice API that also publishes order events.
output: A workflow that separates synchronous endpoint work from event handler work.
Agent responsibilities for schema design, queue setup, implementation, and review.
Monitoring tasks for API metrics and event processing health.

best_practices: Confirm requirements, data ownership, and security needs before starting implementation.
Keep every endpoint inside a visible RED, GREEN, and REFACTOR cycle.
Review deployment commands against the target environment before execution.
anti_patterns: Skipping OpenAPI design and writing endpoints without a shared contract.
Treating generated command examples as production commands without review.
Moving to deployment before security, performance, documentation, and rollback gates pass.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps organize production REST API delivery from planning through deployment and monitoring.

faq.question: Does it write the complete backend code?
faq.answer: No. It coordinates agents and phases. Implementation still depends on project context and available tools.

faq.question: Which development method does it use?
faq.answer: It centers delivery on Test-Driven Development with RED, GREEN, and REFACTOR cycles.

faq.question: Can it support security review?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes security specialist tasks, OWASP API checks, secrets scanning, and release gates.

faq.question: Does it require Kubernetes?
faq.answer: No. Kubernetes appears in examples. Teams can adapt deployment steps to their platform.

faq.question: Is it suitable for small APIs?
faq.answer: Yes, but the workflow may need simplification when the API has low risk or few endpoints.
